items.title: [Bug] MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser: top-level `oneOf` parameters schema not resolved (numbers become strings, arrays leak raw tags)
items.body:
## Checklist
- [x] Searched existing issues
- [x] Reproduced on latest main

## Describe the bug

When a tool's `parameters` uses a top-level `oneOf` (a common JSON-Schema composition), SGLang's
MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser fails to resolve the per-branch property schemas. As a result the emitted
`tool_calls[].function.arguments` have the wrong types:

- a `number` argument is returned as a **string** (`{"number": "42"}` instead of `{"number": 42}`)
- an `array` argument **leaks the model's raw internal parser tags** as a plain string
  (`{"stringList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>..."}` instead of `{"stringList": ["12","34"]}`)

This is caught by MiniMax's official verifier test
`m3_format_check/m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream`.

## Reproduction

Serve MiniMax-M3 with tool-call parsing enabled:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --port 8043
```

Run the official verifier test (from https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Provider-Verifier):

```bash
export M3_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8043
export M3_API_KEY=sk-none
export M3_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3
cd m3_format_check
python3 -m pytest \
  "m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream" -v
```

The test defines a tool whose `parameters` is a top-level `oneOf` with three branches
(`number` / `stringList` / `numberList`) and asks the model to call it three times, once per branch,
with `number=42`, `stringList=["12","34"]`, `numberList=[12,34]`.

## Actual behavior (official verifier output)

```
m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream FAILED

E   AssertionError: oneof toplevel stream: number must be numeric, got str='42'.
    calls=[
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"number": "42"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFuumber": "42"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"stringList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>]<]minimax[>[<item>34]<]minimax[>[</item>"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"numberList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>]<]minimax[>[<item>34]<]minimax[>[</item>"}'}
    ]
```

- `number` → `"42"` (string, should be `42`)
- `stringList` / `numberList` → a string containing raw `]<]minimax[>[<item>...` tags
  (should be `["12","34"]` and `[12,34]`)

## Expected behavior

```json
{"number": 42}
{"stringList": ["12", "34"]}
{"numberList": [12, 34]}
```

## Environment

- SGresent on current main)
- Model: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`

items.title: [Bug] GLM tool-call parser corrupts string arguments that look like numbers with underscores (e.g. "123_456" -> "123456")
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When a model returns a tool call whose string argument is an all-digit value
containing underscores (a very common ID format, e.g. `"123_456"`), the GLM
tool-call parser silently strips the underscores and returns `"123456"`. This
happens **even when the argument is explicitly declared as `"type": "string"` in
the tool schema**.

In practice this creates an infinite retry loop in agentic workloads: the model
correctly emits `<arg_value>123_456</arg_value>`, the tool backend rejects the
mangled `123456` as an invalid ID, the model reasons "I'll retry with the
underscore", emits `123_456` again, and the parser mangles it again — forever. The
same requests work correctly on other backends (e.g. vLLM's GLM parser), which
points to a parser bug rather than a model issue.

### Root cause

In `python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py` (and the duplicated code
in `glm47_moe_detector.py`), `parse_arguments()` uses `ast.literal_eval` as a
fallback strategy:

```python
# Strategy 3: ast.literal_eval
try:
    parsed_value = ast.literal_eval(json_value)
    return parsed_value, True
except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
    pass
```

Because of PEP 515, Python treats underscores in numeric literals as digit-group
separators, so `ast.literal_eval("123_456")` returns the int `123456` (underscore
gone). Then in `_parse_argument_pairs`, even the `arg_type == "string"` branch
cannot recover it, because it stringifies the already-corrupted int:

```python
if arg_type == "string":
    if isinstance(parsed_value, str):
        arguments[arg_key] = parsed_value
    elif isinstance(parsed_value, (dict, list)):
        arguments[arg_key] = json.dumps(parsed_value, ensure_ascii=False)
    else:
        arguments[arg_key] = str(parsed_value)   # str(123456) == "123456"
```

This affects both `Glm4MoeDetector` and `Glm47MoeDetector` (they duplicate the same
`parse_arguments` / `_parse_argument_pairs` logic).

### Expected behavior

String argument values must be preserved verbatim:

- When the schema declares the argument as `"type": "string"`, the raw value should
  be used and never coerced via `ast.literal_eval` / numeric parsing.
- Even without a schema type, a value that only differs from the raw string because
  of PEP-515 underscore collapsing should not be silently converted (`"123_456"`
  should not become `123456`).

### Proposed fix

Two independent guards (either one fixes the reported case; both together is
safest), applied to **both** `glm4_moe_detector.py` and `glm47_moe_detector.py`:

1. Don't let `ast.literal_eval` collapse underscore-containing numeric-looking
   strings:

```python
# Strategy 3: ast.literal_eval
try:
    parsed_value = ast.literal_eval(json_value)
    # PEP 515: "123_456" would collapse to int 123456; keep the raw string.
    if isinstance(parsed_value, (int, float)) and "_" in json_value:
        return json_value, True
    return parsed_value, True
except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
    pass
```

2. For `arg_type == "string"`, use the raw value directly instead of the parsed
   value, so string fields never go through numeric coercion at all.

For reference, vLLM's GLM parser avoids this by checking `_is_string_type()` before
calling `_deserialize()`, so string args are never passed to `ast.literal_eval`.

### Reproduction

Minimal, at the parser-function level:

```python
from sglang.srt.function_call.glm4_moe_detector import parse_arguments

print(parse_arguments("123_456", "string"))
# actual:   (123456, True)
# expected: ("123_456", True)
```

End-to-end at the detector level:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.glm47_moe_detector import Glm47MoeDetector

tools = [
    Tool(
        type="function",
        function=Function(
            name="get_item",
            parameters={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["id"],
            },
        ),
    )
]

text = "<tool_call>get_item<arg_key>id</arg_key><arg_value>123_456</arg_value></tool_call>"
result = Glm47MoeDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools)
print(result.calls[0].parameters)
# actual:   {"id": "123456"}
# expected: {"id": "123_456"}
```

### Environment

items.title: [Bug] KimiK2Detector streaming parser silently drops / hangs on multi-turn tool calls with long arguments (full rewrite proposed)
items.body:
## [Bug] KimiK2Detector streaming parser silently drops / hangs on multi-turn tool calls with long arguments (full rewrite proposed)
### Checklist
- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Related issues
- #8613 — Kimi-K2 incomplete content during multi-turn streaming tool calling
- #18086 — Kimi-k2.5 tool call parser may not work probabilistically
- #10600 — kimi_k2 parser tool-index messup in multi-turn
- #12932 — Kimi-K2-Thinking drops optional parameters after reasoning
- #20878 — Improve Kimi-K2.5 tool parser (regex doesn't allow `-`, missed calls)
- #20688 — content field mixed with function calls
- vllm-project/vllm#37184 — equivalent fix already reviewed and landed in vLLM
### Describe the bug
The current `KimiK2Detector` (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/kimik2_detector.py`) has a fundamental fragility in `parse_streaming_increment` that causes **silent hangs**, **truncated arguments**, and **missed tool calls** when:
- the model emits **multiple tool calls in a single turn** (e.g. `write_to_file` + `execute_command`);
- the generated JSON arguments are **long (>5 KB)** and contain markdown, emoji, backticks or nested braces;
- a special token (`\u8f93` / `*) is **split across chunk boundaries**;
- the detector instance is **reused between requests** and the previous failure leaks state.
The observable symptoms depend on which layer fails:

| Symptom | Affected layer | Typical trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Agent/UI "hangs" forever in `partial: true` | Client (Cline, Roo, Claude Code) | Long JSON args with emoji/newlines; marker split across chunks |
| `functions.*` tokens leak into `content` / `reasoning_content` | Downstream parser | Lazy regex truncates tool call, rest is emitted as normal text |
| Tool call silently dropped, only first of N emitted | Streaming delta assembler | No loop around regex; early-exit after first match |
| `list index out of range` / `Expecting value` in server log | `parse_streaming_increment` | `except` handler leaves `_buffer` in poisoned state |

### Root cause analysis
I instrumented the current `kimik2_detector.py` (the one shipped up to at least 0.5.9) and found **7 structural defects** in the streaming path:
1. **`r"\{.*?\}"` breaks JSON on first `}`**  
   The `tool_call_regex` uses a lazy match that terminates at the *first* closing brace. If the tool argument contains nested JSON, markdown code fences, `{{placeholders}}`, or any literal `}`, the captured arguments are truncated. `_is_complete_json` then returns `False`, and the parser withholds the delta indefinitely.
2. **No rolling / bounded buffer**  
   `self._buffer` grows without limit. On long files (>50 KB) the repeated `self.bot_token in current_text` scan is **O(N²)**. Worse, if the model never emits the closing `` (truncated by `max_tokens` or context limit), the buffer never flushes, becoming a silent memory leak.
3. **Chunk-boundary marker straddle is not handled**  
   When `` (singular, from K2-Thinking) | Accepted as valid end | **Ignored, state stuck** |
| 7 | Unclosed section (run-away) | Safety-valve flush after limit | **Infinite hang** |
| 8 | 1-char-per-chunk torture test (~192 calls) | Stable parse | **Duplicated args** |
| 9 | `\u003c` inside JSON string | Treated as literal, not marker | **Parser confusion** |
| 10 | Empty `{}` arguments | Flushed immediately | OK |
| 11 | Instance reused between requests | Clean slate each time | **State leak** |
| 12 | Non-streaming `detect_and_parse` on turn-39 shape | Full parse | Truncated |
### Expected behavior
- Streaming parser must be **robust to chunk boundaries**: a token split across two SSE deltas must not corrupt state or duplicate output.
- Long arguments with arbitrary markdown must not be truncated by a naive brace-counting regex.
- Multiple tool calls in a single assistant turn must all be emitted.
- A run-away section (no closing marker within a configurable limit) must flush as normal text rather than hang the client.
- State must be fully isolated between requests.
### Proposed fix
A full rewrite of `kimik2_detector.py` is proposed. The implementation is a **straight port** of the vLLM fix that was already reviewed and merged in `vllm-project/vllm#37184` (schema accuracy: 87% → 98–100% on K2-Vendor-Verifier).
Key changes:
- **Replace `r"\{.*?\}"`** with `(?:(?!<\|tool_call_begin\|>).)*?` and anchor on ``  ; this survives nested braces and markdown.
- Add `SGLANG_KIMI_PARSER_SECTION_MAX` (default 512 KB) as a **safety valve** on unclosed sections.
- Introduce a **rolling 256-byte `marker_buffer`** for O(1) boundary detection and marker-stutter protection.
- Support both `tool_calls_section_*` and `tool_call_section_*` markers (K2-Thinking variant).
- Accumulate prefix text in a loop; never swallow it.
- Emit `name` and `args` in the **same chunk** when the full call fits.
- Add an explicit `reset()` path and clear `_buffer` / `_last_arguments` on `except`.
- Keep the public surface unchanged: `has_tool_call`, `detect_and_parse`, `parse_streaming_increment`, `build_ebnf` / `structure_info`.
### Attachments
- `kimik2_detector.py` — proposed replacement (512 lines)
- `test_kimik2_detector.py` — standalone mock harness, 12 scenarios (502 lines)

https://gist.github.com/Dixon3/ff71ef4efa21a70cda84afc3e0b6e885

### Environment
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` (also reproducible on `Kimi-K2-Instruct`) |
| SGLang | 0.5.8, 0.5.9 |
| Parser flags | `--tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --reasoning-parser kimi_k2` |
| Client | Cline, Roo Code, Claude Code, Kilo Code (any agentic client with `stream=true`) |
| HW | 8×H100, 8×H200, 8×B200 — hardware-agnostic |
### Additional context
- `SGLANG_TOOL_STRICT_LEVEL=2` and `xgrammar==0.1.31` **do not** fix these symptoms because the failures happen in `parse_streaming_increment`, not in grammar-constrained generation.
- The same workload with `--tool-call-parser glm47` or `--tool-call-parser qwen25` does **not** hang, confirming the bug is specific to `kimi_k2` detector state machine.
- **Immediate mitigation** for users: disable streaming on the client side for Kimi-K2.5 endpoints (`"stream": false`), or switch to a non-Kimi parser if the model wrapper permits.
---
/cc @JustinTong0323 @yhyang201 @CatherineSue — this is intended to close the long tail of kimi_k2 parser bugs with a single rewrite rather than incremental band-aids.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6 tool call with tool_choice="required" causes </parameter to appear in tool call response
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


When serving Qwen3.6 with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, OpenAI tool calling may behave incorrectly when `tool_choice="required"` is set.

For a simple single-tool request, the model may repeatedly generate the same tool call until `finish_reason="length"`. In some cases, malformed Qwen3-Coder-style parameter end tags are also leaked into the parsed function arguments.

This does not happen when `tool_choice` is omitted. For the same request, using `--tool-call-parser qwen` also returns normally. However, the official Qwen3.6 deployment docs recommend `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`.

Request body:

```json
{
    "model": "qwen3p6-35b-a3b-256k",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "查询上海的天气"
        }
    ],
    "tools": [  
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": "get_weather",
                "description": "获取指定城市的当前天气信息",
                "parameters": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "city": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "城市名称，例如：上海、北京"
                        }
                    },
                    "required": [
                        "city"
                    ]
                }
            }
        }
    ],
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
        "enable_thinking": true
    },
    "tool_choice": "required",
    "max_tokens": 3000,
    "stream": false
}
```

Actual response:

```json

    "id": "65d0cb794c564692a74d0e49ecb15dea",
    "object": "chat.completion",
    "created": 1780618730,

Proceed. \n   - Output matches the required JSON format for tool calling.✅\n   - I will generate the tool call now. \n   - [Proceeds]\n",

Expected response:

```json

```json
{"city": "上海\n</parameter1>\"}
```
or
```json

```
or:
```json

```

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3 Coder buffers large string tool-call arguments during streaming
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

The Qwen3 Coder tool-call parser currently buffers string parameter values until it sees `</parameter>` or another terminating tag.

For large string arguments, such as a `write_file` tool with a long `content` field, this means OpenAI-compatible streaming clients do not receive incremental `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments while the content is being generated. Instead, the whole string argument is emitted as one large chunk only after the closing parameter tag arrives.

This breaks the expected streaming behavior for tool calls with large string fields. Clients that render or process tool-call arguments incrementally cannot observe progress until the full parameter is complete.

### Expected behavior

For string-like parameters, Qwen3 Coder streaming should emit argument fragments progressively as the value arrives, while preserving valid JSON across chunks. For example, after receiving the beginning of a large `content` parameter, the stream should already include something like:

```text
{"content": "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n...
```

before the parser has seen the final `</parameter>` token.

Non-string parameters such as booleans, integers, arrays, and objects can continue using the existing complete-value parsing path.

### Actual behavior

The parser emits the parameter key and value only after the closing parameter tag is seen. With a long `content` value, the client gets one large `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` chunk at the end instead of incremental chunks during generation.

### Reproduction

A minimal parser-level reproduction is a Qwen3 Coder tool call where a string parameter is split across streaming chunks and the closing `</parameter>` tag is delayed or split:

```text
<tool_call>
<function=write_file>
<parameter=file_path>/tmp/demo.html</parameter>
<parameter=content>
<!DOCTYPE html>\n
<html>\n
<body>hello</body>\n
</par
ameter>
<parameter=overwrite>false</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

When these chunks are fed through `Qwen3CoderDetector.parse_streaming_increment`, no incremental `content` argument fragments are emitted before the content parameter closes. The `content` argument is buffered until `</parameter>` is complete.

### Suggested fix

Stream schema string-like parameters incrementally in `Qwen3CoderDetector`, while keeping the existing complete-value path for non-string parameters.

A proposed implementation and regression test are already available in PR #25246:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25246

That PR verifies that a long `content` parameter emits before `</parameter>` is received, and that the final accumulated JSON remains valid.

### Environment

This is a parser-only issue in the Qwen3 Coder function-call detector. It does not depend on CUDA kernels, model forward execution, scheduling, or token generation speed.

Observed against the current `main` branch behavior before PR #25246.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Kimi-K2.5 keeps spitting out these weird tokens that break the JSON structure. When it happens, some apps like Kilo crash right away, while others like Opencode just stop responding instead of retrying like they should.

```python
MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_TOKENS = frozenset(
    {"<|tool_calls_section_begin|>", " <|tool_call_begin|>", "<|tool_call_argument_begin|>"}
)
```

Just to be clear, this isn't about the model sending invalid tool parameters or missing/multiple arguments. Those are actually catchable issues because the model still outputs a valid JSON structure. Coding agents can usually handle this signal and send back guidance to help the model self-heal.

The problem here is different: the model's output isn't valid JSON syntax at all. In some tools, this bad "message" gets stuck in the history log and can't be removed, which causes all retries to fail (like in Kilo). Other tools just swallow the error entirely since it doesn't match any expected error type, so no recovery mechanism triggers, leading to a dropped session (like in Opencode). Luckily, when those tools retry, they automatically restore the session and remove that broken -1 message.

I can't quite tell where the issue is. How should I fix it to get things running smoothly again?

### Reproduction

just chat

```yaml

items.title: [Feature] Add tool call accuracy tests for large models to nightly CI
items.body:
## Motivation

Tool call tests today only cover a small model (Llama-3.2-1B in `test/registered/openai_server/function_call/test_openai_function_calling.py`). Large models like DeepSeek V3.2 have no tool call coverage in CI, so bugs like #17593 and #17551 only get caught when users hit them. This issue tracks adding tool call tests to the nightly 8-GPU suite.

## Scenarios

These should be common across all models that support tool calling:

**Basic**
1. Format check — `tool_calls` is a non-empty list, `function.name` / `function.arguments` present, arguments is valid JSON, `finish_reason` is `"tool_calls"`
2. Field placement — tool call goes in `tool_calls`, not `content` (#17593)
3. Streaming — chunks concatenate to valid JSON, `finish_reason` correct

**tool_choice**

4. `"required"` — always returns tool call
5. `"none"` — never returns tool call
6. Specific function — returns the specified one

**Multi-turn**

7. Tool result follow-up — pass tool result back, model replies based on it
8. Thinking + tool call — after tool result, output in `content` not `reasoning_content` (#17551, DeepSeek specific for now — might be model-internal, will write the test first and see)

**Other**

9. Parallel tool calls — multiple tool calls in one request
10. Strict mode — `strict: true` enforces schema

## CI integration

Add to `test/registered/8-gpu-models/test_deepseek_v32.py`, two variants:

Non-MTP:
```
--tp=8 --dp=8 --enable-dp-attention
--tool-call-parser deepseekv32
--reasoning-parser deepseek-v3
```

MTP (speculative decoding):
```
same as above +
--speculative-algorithm=EAGLE
--speculative-num-steps=3
--speculative-eagle-topk=1
--speculative-num-draft-tokens=4
env: SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
```

Both in `nightly-8-gpu-common`.

## Plan

Start with DeepSeek V3.2, then extend to GLM / Qwen / others reusing the same scenarios.

## Refs

- Small model tests: `test/registered/openai_server/function_call/test_openai_function_calling.py`
- Parser tests: `test/registered/function_call/test_parallel_tool_calls.py`
- #17593, #17551

items.title: [Bug] `kimi_k2` tool-call parser produces invalid JSON escape sequences when streaming
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When using `--tool-call-parser kimi_k2` with `stream: true`, the SSE `tool_calls[].function.arguments` chunks produce concatenated JSON that contains invalid escape sequences (e.g. `\(`, `\|`, `\'`). The same request with `stream: false` returns valid JSON.

This is a **streaming-only** bug — the chunking path in the parser corrupts backslash escape sequences, likely by splitting `\\` pairs across chunk boundaries so that one `\` ends up at the end of one chunk and the character after it (e.g. `(`, `|`, `'`) starts the next, producing an invalid JSON escape in the concatenated result.

### Observed behavior

Concatenating the streamed `tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments produces a string that fails `json.loads()` with errors like:

```
Invalid \escape: line 1 column 10491 (char 10490)
```

### Evidence for the streaming parser bug (A=FAIL, B=PASS)

The critical run that isolates the parser bug:

```
  A (stream + tools)    : FAIL
  B (non-stream + tools): PASS    ← model JSON is valid
  C (stream, no tools)  : PASS

  -> STREAMING PARSER BUG: model produced valid JSON (B=PASS)
     but the streaming chunking path corrupted it (A=FAIL).
```

Inspecting the raw SSE chunks from a failing streaming response shows the parser splits `\\` escape pairs across chunk boundaries. For example:

| Chunk | SSE `arguments` value | Decoded fragment |
|-------|----------------------|------------------|
| N     | `"\\\\"` | `\\` |
| N+1   | `".\\"` | `.\` |
| N+2   | `"("` | `(` |

Concatenated: `\\.\(` — where `\\.` is valid (escaped backslash + dot) but `\(` is an invalid JSON escape. The model's original output had `\\.\\(` (both properly escaped), but the streaming chunker lost a backslash.

### Evidence for the model inconsistency (A=FAIL, B=FAIL, C=FAIL)

Sometimes the model itself generates inconsistent escaping:

```
  A (stream + tools)    : FAIL
  B (non-stream + tools): FAIL    ← model JSON is ALSO invalid
  C (stream, no tools)  : FAIL

  -> MODEL BUG (this run): model produced invalid JSON in all modes.
```

Inspecting the non-streaming response at the error position shows the model correctly escapes some backslashes but not others in the same string:

```
sed -n 's/.*mesh.*=.*\\[\([0-9,[:space:]]*\\)\\].*/\\1/p'
                       ^^                  ^^  ^^  <- correctly escaped (\\)
                         ^^                        <- NOT escaped (\()
```

This is a separate model-level issue (inconsistent JSON escaping of BRE regex patterns).

### Expected behavior

Streaming `tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments should concatenate to valid JSON, identical to the non-streaming `stream: false` response. The streaming path should not corrupt the model's output.

### Likely root cause

The streaming code path in the `kimi_k2` tool-call parser splits the model's raw output into chunks without ensuring that JSON `\\` escape sequences are kept atomic. When a `\\` pair lands at a chunk boundary, one `\` ends up at the end of chunk N and the next character starts chunk N+1, producing an invalid escape in the concatenated result.

### Reproduction

The bug triggers when the model generates long tool-call arguments containing bash scripts with BRE regex patterns (backslash-heavy content like `grep -rn 'dist\.\(all_reduce\|all_gather\)'`). It is intermittent — roughly 30-60% of streaming requests fail.

**Self-contained repro script** (zero dependencies beyond stdlib). The script runs an A/B/C diagnostic to distinguish parser vs model issues, then repeats streaming attempts to demonstrate intermittency:
**Self-contained repro script** (zero dependencies beyond stdlib):

<details>
<summary>test_kimi_k2_streaming_tool_calls.py (click to expand)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Repro: kimi_k2 tool-call parser produces invalid JSON when streaming.

The streaming SSE output from --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 contains
tool_call argument chunks whose concatenation has broken JSON escape
sequences (e.g. \\( \\| \\' instead of \\\\( \\\\| \\\\').

This is a *streaming-only* parser bug:
  - stream=true  + tools  → FAILS  (argument JSON is corrupted)
  - stream=false + tools  → PASSES (same parser, no chunking)
  - stream=true, no tools → PASSES (model's raw JSON output is fine)

The script runs an A/B/C comparison to confirm the diagnosis, then
optionally repeats mode A several times to demonstrate intermittency.

Requires a running sglang server with --tool-call-parser kimi_k2.

Usage:
    python test_kimi_k2_streaming_tool_calls.py <model> [--endpoint URL] [--attempts N]

Examples:
    python test_kimi_k2_streaming_tool_calls.py nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4
    python test_kimi_k2_streaming_tool_calls.py moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5 --endpoint http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions
    python test_kimi_k2_streaming_tool_calls.py nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 --attempts 5
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

# ── prompts & schema ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

TOOL_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "run_bash",
        "description": "Run a bash command",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "script":               {"type": "string",  "description": "The bash command to run"},
                "timeout":              {"type": "integer", "description": "Seconds before timeout"},
                "description":          {"type": "string",  "description": "Clear description"},
                "risk":                 {"type": "string",  "enum": ["low", "medium", "high"]},
                "mutation_kind":        {"type": "string",  "enum": ["none", "create", "edit", "overwrite", "append", "delete"]},
                "mutation_targets":     {"type": "array",   "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "File paths"},
                "affects_shared_state": {"type": "boolean"},
                "enable_llm_parser":    {"type": "boolean"},
            },
            "required": ["script", "timeout", "description", "risk", "mutation_kind",
                         "mutation_targets", "affects_shared_state", "enable_llm_parser"],
        },
    },
}

# Prompt that makes the model generate bash scripts containing BRE regex
# patterns with backslash-paren/pipe/dot — the sequences that break.
TOOL_PROMPT = (
    "You are an ML infrastructure engineer. Generate exactly 1 run_bash tool call. "
    "The 'script' field must contain a bash script (80+ lines) that uses grep with "
    "basic regex (BRE) patterns to audit a distributed training codebase. "
    "The script MUST use:\n"
    "  - grep with escaped parens and pipes, e.g.: "
    r"grep -rn 'dist\.\(all_reduce\|all_gather\|reduce_scatter\)'" "\n"
    "  - find with -regex using escaped special chars\n"
    "  - sed with capture groups using escaped parens\n"
    "  - associative arrays, trap handlers, heredocs, temp file management\n"
    "  - extensive inline comments explaining each command\n\n"
    "The 'description' field must be a detailed technical essay (2000+ words) "
    "covering parallelism strategies, NCCL collectives, device mesh configs, "
    "ZeRO optimization, NVLink topology, and how this script fits into a broader "
    "distributed training audit workflow.\n\n"
    "The 'mutation_targets' array should list 15+ file paths.\n"
    "IMPORTANT: use MANY BRE-style escaped parens and pipes in grep/sed patterns."
)

# Same intent, but for mode C: raw content output, no tool calling.
CONTENT_PROMPT = (
    "You are an ML infrastructure engineer. Output a JSON object (NOT a tool "
    "call — just raw JSON as text) with these fields:\n"
    '  - "script": a bash script (80+ lines) that uses grep with BRE patterns '
    "to audit a distributed training codebase. Use:\n"
    "    - grep with escaped parens/pipes, e.g.: "
    r"grep -rn 'dist\.\(all_reduce\|all_gather\|reduce_scatter\)'" "\n"
    "    - find with -regex, sed with capture groups\n"
    "    - associative arrays, trap handlers, heredocs\n"
    '  - "description": a technical essay (2000+ words) on parallelism strategies\n'
    '  - "mutation_targets": array of 15+ file paths\n\n'
    "Output ONLY the JSON object, no markdown fences. "
    "Use MANY BRE-style escaped parens and pipes in the grep/sed patterns."
)

# ── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def find_bad_escapes(s: str, limit: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
    """Find truly invalid JSON escape sequences, accounting for \\\\ pairs."""
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(s) - 1:
        if s[i] == '\\':
            next_ch = s[i + 1]
            if next_ch == '\\':
                i += 2  # valid \\\\ pair, skip both
                continue
            if next_ch not in '"/bfnrtu':
                lo, hi = max(0, i - 30), min(len(s), i + 20)
                out.append({"pos": i, "esc": s[i:i+2], "ctx": s[lo:hi]})
                if len(out) >= limit:
                    break
            i += 2  # skip the escape sequence
        else:
            i += 1
    return out


def check_json(s: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None, list[dict]]:
    """Return (valid, error_msg_or_None, bad_escapes)."""
    try:
        json.loads(s)
        return True, None, find_bad_escapes(s)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        return False, str(e), find_bad_escapes(s)


def post(endpoint: str, payload: dict) -> urllib.request.http.client.HTTPResponse:
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        endpoint,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req)


def collect_streaming_tool_calls(resp) -> tuple[dict[int, dict], str | None]:
    tool_calls: dict[int, dict] = {}
    finish_reason = None
    with resp:
        for raw_line in resp:
            line = raw_line.decode().strip()
            if not line.startswith("data:"):
                continue
            raw = line[5:].strip()
            if raw == "[DONE]":
                break
            try:
                chunk = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            choices = chunk.get("choices", [])
            if not choices:
                continue
            choice = choices[0]
            if choice.get("finish_reason"):
                finish_reason = choice["finish_reason"]
            delta = choice.get("delta") or {}
            for tc in delta.get("tool_calls") or []:
                idx = tc["index"]
                if idx not in tool_calls:
                    tool_calls[idx] = {"id": None, "name": None, "chunks": []}
                if tc.get("id"):
                    tool_calls[idx]["id"] = tc["id"]
                fn = tc.get("function") or {}
                if fn.get("name"):
                    tool_calls[idx]["name"] = fn["name"]
                if fn.get("arguments"):
                    tool_calls[idx]["chunks"].append(fn["arguments"])
    return tool_calls, finish_reason


def collect_streaming_content(resp) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    chunks, finish_reason = [], None
    with resp:
        for raw_line in resp:
            line = raw_line.decode().strip()
            if not line.startswith("data:"):
                continue
            raw = line[5:].strip()
            if raw == "[DONE]":
                break
            try:
                chunk = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            choices = chunk.get("choices", [])
            if not choices:
                continue
            choice = choices[0]
            if choice.get("finish_reason"):
                finish_reason = choice["finish_reason"]
            delta = choice.get("delta") or {}
            if delta.get("content"):
                chunks.append(delta["content"])
    return "".join(chunks), finish_reason

# ── modes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def mode_a(endpoint: str, model: str) -> dict:
    """stream=true + tools (through kimi_k2 parser, chunked SSE)."""
    resp = post(endpoint, {"stream": True, "model": model,
                           "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": TOOL_PROMPT}],
                           "tools": [TOOL_SCHEMA]})
    tcs, finish = collect_streaming_tool_calls(resp)
    results = []
    for idx in sorted(tcs):
        args_str = "".join(tcs[idx]["chunks"])
        ok, err, bad = check_json(args_str)
        results.append({"len": len(args_str), "valid": ok, "error": err, "bad": bad})
    return {"mode": "A  stream + tools", "finish": finish,
            "n_tool_calls": len(tcs), "results": results}


def mode_b(endpoint: str, model: str) -> dict:
    """stream=false + tools (same parser, NOT chunked)."""
    resp = post(endpoint, {"stream": False, "model": model,
                           "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": TOOL_PROMPT}],
                           "tools": [TOOL_SCHEMA]})
    body = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
    choices = body.get("choices", [])
    if not choices:
        return {"mode": "B  non-stream + tools", "finish": None,
                "n_tool_calls": 0, "results": []}
    choice = choices[0]
    tcs = choice.get("message", {}).get("tool_calls", [])
    results = []
    for tc in tcs:
        args_str = tc.get("function", {}).get("arguments", "")
        ok, err, bad = check_json(args_str)
        results.append({"len": len(args_str), "valid": ok, "error": err, "bad": bad})
    return {"mode": "B  non-stream + tools", "finish": choice.get("finish_reason"),
            "n_tool_calls": len(tcs), "results": results}


def mode_c(endpoint: str, model: str) -> dict:
    """stream=true, NO tools (bypasses tool-call parser entirely)."""
    resp = post(endpoint, {"stream": True, "model": model,
                           "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": CONTENT_PROMPT}]})
    content, finish = collect_streaming_content(resp)
    json_str = content.strip()
    if json_str.startswith("```"):
        lines = json_str.split("\n")[1:]
        if lines and lines[-1].strip() == "```":
            lines = lines[:-1]
        json_str = "\n".join(lines)
    ok, err, bad = check_json(json_str)
    return {"mode": "C  stream, no tools", "finish": finish,
            "content_len": len(content),
            "results": [{"len": len(json_str), "valid": ok, "error": err, "bad": bad}]}

# ── display ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def print_result(res: dict):
    print(f"\n{'─'*60}")
    print(f"  {res['mode']}")
    print(f"  finish_reason: {res.get('finish')}", end="")
    if "n_tool_calls" in res:
        print(f"  |  tool_calls: {res['n_tool_calls']}", end="")
    if "content_len" in res:
        print(f"  |  content: {res['content_len']} chars", end="")
    print()
    for i, r in enumerate(res.get("results", [])):
        tag = "VALID" if r["valid"] else "INVALID"
        print(f"  [{i}] {r['len']:>6d} chars  {tag}")
        if not r["valid"]:
            print(f"      error: {r['error']}")
            if r.get("bad"):
                for be in r["bad"]:
                    print(f"      bad escape at {be['pos']}: {be['esc']!r}  ...{be['ctx']}...")

# ── main ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Repro for kimi_k2 streaming tool-call JSON corruption bug")
    ap.add_argument("model", help="Model name, e.g. nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4")
    ap.add_argument("--endpoint", default="http://localhost:10001/v1/chat/completions")
    ap.add_argument("--attempts", type=int, default=3,
                    help="Extra mode-A repetitions after the A/B/C comparison (default: 3)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    print(f"Model    : {args.model}")
    print(f"Endpoint : {args.endpoint}")
    print()
    print("Phase 1 — A/B/C comparison (isolate parser vs model)")
    print("=" * 60)

    abc = {}
    for label, fn in [("A", mode_a), ("B", mode_b), ("C", mode_c)]:
        print(f"\n>>> Mode {label} ...")
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            res = fn(args.endpoint, args.model)
        except Exception as e:
            res = {"mode": label, "results": [
                {"len": 0, "valid": False, "error": str(e), "bad": []}]}
        print(f"    {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", end="")
        print_result(res)
        abc[label] = res

    a_ok = all(r["valid"] for r in abc["A"]["results"])
    b_ok = all(r["valid"] for r in abc["B"]["results"])
    c_ok = all(r["valid"] for r in abc["C"]["results"])

    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"  A (stream + tools)    : {'PASS' if a_ok else 'FAIL'}")
    print(f"  B (non-stream + tools): {'PASS' if b_ok else 'FAIL'}")
    print(f"  C (stream, no tools)  : {'PASS' if c_ok else 'FAIL'}")
    print()
    if not a_ok and b_ok:
        print("  -> STREAMING PARSER BUG: model produced valid JSON (B=PASS)")
        print("     but the streaming chunking path corrupted it (A=FAIL).")
    elif not a_ok and not b_ok and c_ok:
        print("  -> PARSER BUG (non-chunking): both stream/non-stream tool calls fail,")
        print("     but raw content is fine.")
    elif not a_ok and not b_ok and not c_ok:

  def get_structure_constraint(

```python
def build_structural_tag(
    self,
    tools: List[Tool],
    at_least_one: bool = False,
    stop_after_first: bool = False,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Build structural tag for [MODEL] format."""
    tags = []
    triggers = set()

    for tool in tools:
        name = tool.function.name
        if not name:
            continue

        # Define model-specific format
        begin = "..."  # From old structure_info()
        end = "..."    # From old structure_info()
        trigger = "..." # From old structure_info()

        # Always include schema
        schema = tool.function.parameters or {}

        tags.append({
            "format": "tag",
            "begin": begin,
            "content": {
                "format": "json_schema",
                "schema": schema
            },
            "end": end
        })

        triggers.add(trigger)

    return {
        "format": "triggered_tags",
        "triggers": list(triggers),
        "tags": tags,
        "at_least_one": at_least_one,
        "stop_after_first": stop_after_first
    }
```

**For DeepSeek detectors** (wrapper tags format):

```python
def build_structural_tag(
    self,
    tools: List[Tool],
    at_least_one: bool = False,
    stop_after_first: bool = False,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Build structural tag for DeepSeek wrapper format."""
    # Build individual tool call tags
    tool_tags = []
    for tool in tools:
        name = tool.function.name
        if not name:
            continue

        schema = tool.function.parameters or {}

        tool_tags.append({
            "format": "tag",
            "begin": "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>\n```jsonc\n{",
            "content": {
                "format": "json_schema",
                "schema": schema
            },
            "end": "}\n```\n<｜tool▁call▁end｜>"
        })

    # Wrap in outer tag with separator
    return {
        "format": "triggered_tags",
        "triggers": ["<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>"],
        "tags": [{
            "format": "tag",
            "begin": "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>\n",
            "content": {
                "format": "tags_with_separator",
                "tags": tool_tags,
                "separator": "\n",
                "at_least_one": at_least_one,
                "stop_after_first": stop_after_first
            },
            "end": "\n<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>"
        }],
        "at_least_one": False,  # Outer level
        "stop_after_first": False
    }
```

**For Qwen3Coder** (XML parameter format):

```python
def build_structural_tag(
    self,
    tools: List[Tool],
    at_least_one: bool = False,
    stop_after_first: bool = False,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Build structural tag for Qwen3-Coder XML format."""
    tags = []

    for tool in tools:
        name = tool.function.name
        if not name:
            continue

        # Qwen3-Coder uses XML parameter format
        # This may require a custom xgrammar format or schema transformation
        # Refer to: https://xgrammar.mlc.ai/docs/tutorials/structural_tag.html

        schema = tool.function.parameters or {}
        # TODO: May need to transform JSON schema to XML parameter schema

        tags.append({
            "format": "tag",
            "begin": f"<tool_call>\n<name>{name}</name>\n",
            "content": {
                "format": "xml_parameters",  # May need custom format
                "schema": schema
            },
            "end": "\n</tool_call>"
        })

        triggers.add("<tool_call>")

    return {
        "format": "triggered_tags",
        "triggers": list(triggers),
        "tags": tags,
        "at_least_one": at_least_one,
        "stop_after_first": stop_after_first
    }

items.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When using the SGLang Engine to perform inference with the DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus model, if you first run a simple calculation like `2 + 2` and then proceed to a search-based question that requires tool calls, the latter will fail to invoke tools normally.

The expected result is:
```shell
========== Test 1: Simple prompt ==========
Simple output:
4

========== Test 2: Tool call test ==========
============================================================
Generated text:
============================================================
I need to break this down into several steps to solve this puzzle. Let me create a plan:

1. Identify the "prominent hillside school in the Scottish capital designed during the 1820s by a leading Greek Revivalist who helped found a national academy in that decade" and find its construction span, then take the later year
2. Identify the "Anglican parish whose tower base dates to the early 1300s and which was rebuilt in a classical revival idiom in the 1700s" and find the number of Commonwealth World War I burials in its churchyard
3. Identify the "mid-15th-century year when the Habsburg archducal title was officially recognized"
4. Perform the calculation: (later school construction year) + (number of WWI burials) - (Habsburg archducal title year)

Let me start with step 1 - finding the hillside school in Edinburgh.

<use_mcp_tool>
<server_name>search_and_scrape_webpage</server_name>
<tool_name>google_search</tool_name>
<arguments>
{
"q": "prominent hillside school Edinburgh designed 1820s Greek Revivalist founded national academy 1820s"
}
</arguments>
</use_mcp_tool>
============================================================
```

However, the actual output is:
```shell
========== Test 1: Simple prompt ==========
Simple output:
4

========== Test 2: Tool call test ==========
============================================================
Generated text:
============================================================
Let's break this down step by step.

---

**Step 1 – Identify the "prominent hillside school in the Scottish capital designed during the 1820s by a leading Greek Revivalist who helped found a national academy in that decade."**

- Scottish capital = Edinburgh.
- Hillside school = likely the Royal High School (originally on Calton Hill).
- Greek Revival architect in 1820s = Thomas Hamilton (1784–1858).
- Thomas Hamilton helped found the Royal Scottish Academy in 1826.
- The Royal High School building on Calton Hill was designed 1825–1829, built 1826–1829.
- Later year in construction span = **1829**.

---

**Step 2 – Identify the "Anglican parish church whose tower base dates to the early 1300s and which was rebuilt in a classical revival idiom in the 1700s," and find the number of Commonwealth World War I burials in its churchyard.**

- Anglican parish church in the UK with a tower base from early 1300s, classical revival rebuild in 1700s.
- St. Mary’s Church, Battersea, London fits: 13th-century tower base, rebuilt 1775–1777 in classical style by Joseph Dixon.
- Check CWGC records: St. Mary’s, Battersea churchyard has Commonwealth WWI burials.
- CWGC lists **8** WWI burials in St. Mary’s Churchyard, Battersea.

---

**Step 3 – Identify the "mid-15th-century year when the Habsburg archducal title was officially recognized."**

- Habsburg archducal title: Privilegium Maius (forged but declared valid) in 1453 by Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor.
- Official recognition year = **1453**.

---

**Step 4 – Calculate.**

\[
1829 + 8 - 1453 = 384
\]

---

**Final answer:**
\[
\boxed{384}
\]
============================================================
```

Another interesting observation is that after running the first prompt, if you perform a cache flush (engine.flush_cache()), the inference result for the search-based question becomes correct — yet the behavior and outcome remain puzzling.




### Reproduction

```python
"""
Test DeepSeek-V3.1 with sgl.Engine

Usage:
    RANK=$RANK MASTER_ADDR=$MASTER_ADDR python test_sglang_engine_dpskv3.1.py \
    --model-path /mnt/infra/shared_model/DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus-BF16-61layers \
    --enable-memory-saver \
    --simple \
    --tp-size 16 \
    --nnodes 2

import dataclasses

items.title: [Feature] Design Investigation: Custom Function Tool Support in v1/responses API
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Problem Statement

The `v1/responses` API endpoint in SGLang's OpenAI-compatible server currently has **limited tool support**:
- Only supports built-in tools: `"web_search_preview"` and `"code_interpreter"`
- Custom function tools (like `get_weather`, `get_horoscope`) are **not supported for all current models**
- This creates friction for developers using reasoning models who want tool calling capabilities

As noted in OpenAI's documentation:
> "Responses preserves the model's reasoning state across those turns. In Chat Completions, reasoning is dropped between calls"

## Key Files Involved

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0e8a996304383b857adae8357149606b48d08c9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L927-L932 | `ResponseTool` class - **only allows 2 types** |
| [ `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0e8a996304383b857adae8357149606b48d08c9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py) | Main handler - **no FunctionCallParser** |
| [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:880-957`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8308cd36325daf2faea8e66dc8e67b21599c3616/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L880) | Reference implementation with full tool support |
| [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py:86-115`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8308cd36325daf2faea8e66dc8e67b21599c3616/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py#L86) | Harmony model tool handling (has function support) |

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. `ResponseTool` schema is too restrictive

**File**: [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py` (lines 927-932)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0e8a996304383b857adae8357149606b48d08c9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L927-L932)

```python
class ResponseTool(BaseModel):
    """Tool definition for responses."""
    type: Literal["web_search_preview", "code_interpreter"] = Field(
        description="Type of tool to enable"
    )
```

**Problem**: The `type` field only accepts two literal values, preventing custom function tools.

**Expected (per OpenAI Responses API spec)**:
```python
class ResponseTool(BaseModel):
    """Tool definition for responses."""
    type: Literal["function", "web_search_preview", "code_interpreter"] = Field(...)
    # Function tool fields
    name: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    strict: Optional[bool] = None
```

### 2. No `FunctionCallParser` integration in serving_responses.py

**File**: [ `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e0e8a996304383b857adae8357149606b48d08c9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py) 

A grep for `FunctionCallParser` in this file returns **no matches**. The responses handler never attempts to parse tool calls from model output for non-harmony models.

Compare to [serving_chat.py (lines 880-957)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L880):
```python
def _process_tool_calls(self, text, tools, finish_reason, ...):
    # Uses FunctionCallParser to detect and extract tool calls
    parser = FunctionCallParser(tools, self.tool_call_parser)
    if parser.has_tool_call(text):
        text, call_info_list = parser.parse_non_stream(text)
        # ... create tool call objects
```

## Router vs Python Server Comparison

The **router (Rust implementation)** already has full function tool support:

**File**: [`sgl-router/src/protocols/responses.rs` (lines 62-69)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/sgl-router/src/protocols/responses.rs#L64-L69)
```rust
pub enum ResponseToolType {
    Function,           // ✅ Supports custom functions
    WebSearchPreview,
    CodeInterpreter,
    Mcp,
}
```

The router also has complete test coverage:
- [`sgl-router/py_test/e2e_response_api/features/test_function_call.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/sgl-router/py_test/e2e_response_api/features/test_function_call.py)
- [`sgl-router/tests/spec/responses.rs` (lines 631-729)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/sgl-router/tests/spec/responses.rs#L631-L766)

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Update `ResponseTool` schema

**File**: [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py)

```python
class ResponseTool(BaseModel):
    """Tool definition for responses."""
    type: Literal["function", "web_search_preview", "code_interpreter", "mcp"] = Field(
        description="Type of tool to enable"
    )
    # Function tool fields (only used when type == "function")
    name: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Function name")
    description: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Function description")
    parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = Field(default=None, description="JSON Schema for parameters")
    strict: Optional[bool] = Field(default=None, description="Enable strict mode")

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def validate_function_fields(self):
        if self.type == "function" and not self.name:
            raise ValueError("Function tool requires 'name' field")
        return self
```

### Step 2: Add `FunctionCallParser` to [serving_responses.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py)

**Add imports**:
```python
from sglang.srt.parser.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser
```

**Update `_make_response_output_items()` method**:
```python
def _make_response_output_items(self, request, final_output, tokenizer):
    # ... existing reasoning parsing ...

    # NEW: Check for function tools and parse tool calls
    function_tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.type == "function"]
    if function_tools and self.tool_call_parser:
        parser = FunctionCallParser(function_tools, self.tool_call_parser)
        if parser.has_tool_call(content):
            content, call_info_list = parser.parse_non_stream(content)
            for call_info in call_info_list:
                tool_call = ResponseFunctionToolCall(
                    id=f"call_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}",
                    call_id=f"call_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}",
                    type="function_call",
                    name=call_info.name,
                    arguments=call_info.parameters,
                )
                output_items.append(tool_call)

    # ... existing message output creation ...
```

### Step 3: Handle tool choice modes

**Current limitation** [(lines 418-421)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py#L418-L421):
```python
if request.tool_choice != "auto":
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "Only 'auto' tool_choice is supported in response API"
    )
```

**Add support for**:
- `"required"` - Force tool calling (use `JsonArrayParser`)
- `"none"` - Disable tool calling
- Named tool choice - Force specific function

### Step 4: Update ResponsesRequest validation

Ensure tools list is properly validated:
```python
tools: List[ResponseTool] = Field(default_factory=list)

@model_validator(mode='after')
def validate_tools(self):
    for tool in self.tools:
        if tool.type == "function" and not tool.name:
            raise ValueError("Function tool requires name")
    return self
```

## Test Cases to Add

Based on [`sgl-router/py_test/e2e_response_api/features/test_function_call.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/sgl-router/py_test/e2e_response_api/features/test_function_call.py):

1. **Basic function call**: Model returns `function_call` output
2. **Multi-turn with function output**: Provide `function_call_output` and get response
3. **Multiple function tools**: Test with multiple tools defined
4. **Streaming function calls**: Test streaming with function call events
5. **Parallel tool calls**: Test `parallel_tool_calls` parameter

## Files to Modify

1. [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a0d9f6cdd8e2895c30ae74d4e6dc764621bde0b9/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py)
   - Expand `ResponseTool` class
   - Add validation

2. [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a9b8b8457d0674f8d66763fec574fead59e0286/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py#L4)
   - Import `FunctionCallParser`
   - Update `_make_response_output_items()`
   - Update `_make_streaming_response_output_items()` (for streaming)
   - Add tool choice handling

3. `test/per_commit/function_call/test_responses_function_call.py` (new file)
   - Port tests from router implementation

## Related Work

- Router implementation: [`sgl-router/src/routers/openai/responses.rs`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a9b8b8457d0674f8d66763fec574fead59e0286/sgl-router/src/routers/openai/responses.rs#L4)
- Chat completions tool support: [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py:880-1099`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a9b8b8457d0674f8d66763fec574fead59e0286/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L880-L1143)
- Harmony utils (reference): [`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py:86-115`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a9b8b8457d0674f8d66763fec574fead59e0286/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/harmony_utils.py#L86-L115)

### Related resources

- https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses
- https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses

items.title: [Bug] Tool choice `"required"` causes infinite generation for GLM-4.x
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

GLM-4.x consistently enters a seemingly-infinite generation (and consistently has EAGLE multi-token prediction failure, i.e. `accept len: 1.0`) when `tool_choice` is set to `"required"`.

I believe this is because SGLang automatically enforces using the `JsonArrayParser` when `tool_choice` is set to `"required"`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6cfe9f1972d351400f0e56acc55d0af4ef3bc10/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L1050-L1054

Unfortunately, this is incorrect behavior, at least as far as GLM is concerned. GLM *does not use JSON* for tool calls: instead, it uses its own XML-based format, as documented here:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f6cfe9f1972d351400f0e56acc55d0af4ef3bc10/python/sglang/srt/function_call/glm4_moe_detector.py#L46-L50

So attempting to enforce JSON output for tool calls puts the model out of distribution, and also causes the speculator to fail, since it wasn't trained on JSON tool calls (since GLM-4-MoE doesn't use them).

I suspect this is also broken for named function calling (aka, `ToolChoice` — where the caller is forcing a specific function to be called) since it's still trying to force an XML-based tool calling model into responding with JSON; and it's probably also broken for MiniMax M2, which also uses XML rather than JSON. In general it seems unsafe to assume that function/tool calls will be JSON-based for all models: `JsonArrayParser` should probably only be used for `response_format: "json_object"`.

cc @CatherineSue or @TJ5 who might be familiar with the tool calling codepaths.

### Reproduction

Simplified copy from Claude Code, edited to have tool choice set to `required`:

```bash
curl localhost:8000 -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "zai-org/GLM-4.6-FP8",

      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "run a quick git status for me"

    }
  ],
  "stream": false,
  "tool_choice": "required",
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "Bash",
        "description": "Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "command": {
              "type": "string",
              "description": "The command to execute"

            "timeout": {
              "type": "number",
              "description": "Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000)"
            },
            "description": {
              "type": "string",
              "description": "Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words, in active voice. Examples:\nInput: ls\nOutput: List files in current directory\n\nInput: git status\nOutput: Show working tree status\n\nInput: npm install\nOutput: Install package dependencies\n\nInput: mkdir foo\nOutput: Create directory 'foo'"
            },
            "run_in_background": {
              "type": "boolean",

}'
